subject: Trace-to-Alert activation: Observability & Ops activation plan
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Singh <j.singh@asteria-retail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Trace-to-Alert activation: Observability & Ops activation plan

Hi Jared / Priya —

Thanks again for the kickoff yesterday. Per our conversation, I’m sending a short activation plan to get Asteria’s observability handoff moving. Primary goals: deliver a dashboard baseline for production traffic, add lightweight tracing hooks for the top 8 services, define an error taxonomy for downstream routing, and wire alert routing/runbooks to your on-call pager.

Proposed 4–week cadence (high level):
- Week 0 (this week): stakeholder handoff + service inventory + access (Datadog/Splunk / PagerDuty)
- Week 1: tracing hook rollout + example spans (non-blocking canary)
- Week 2: dashboards and SLO guardrails + error taxonomy signoff
- Week 3: alert routing, runbook drafts, and simulated paging exercise

Immediate asks from your side:
1) A service inventory CSV (service name, owner, language, endpoint) — ideally by Mon 17 May
2) PagerDuty team / escalation policy we should target
3) Any compliance constraints (retention, redaction) we should bake into dashboards

I attached a short kickstart checklist and a first-pass tracing patch with recommended span names (tracing_hooks_v1.patch). Laura and Neha will lead the technical runbooks. I’ll coordinate milestones and keep the exec updates succinct.

Proposed next step: 30m implementation planning call — Tue 18 May 10:00–10:30 PT or Wed 19 May 2:00–2:30 PT. Which works for you?

Thanks,
Markus
Head of Customer Success (SMB)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-observability-kickstart-checklist.pdf (4 pages), tracing_hooks_v1.patch (diff, 12kb)

From: Jared Singh <j.singh@asteria-retail.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@asteria-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trace-to-Alert activation: Observability & Ops activation plan

Thanks Markus — this looks good.

Quick answers: we’ll export the service inventory from our internal registry and aim to have it to you by end of day Mon 17 May. PagerDuty: team is "Retail-Platform-Prod" with a two-stage escalation (on-call -> manager). I’ll share the team alias and escalation policy after I confirm with our ops lead (Priya copied).

Two questions up front:
- Are the tracing hooks language-agnostic? we run Node, Go, and a small Python batch.
- For dashboards, do you provide a set of templated panels we can apply, or do you expect us to build from scratch?

Tue 18 May 10:00 PT works for me — will block it on my calendar.

Jared
Head of Platform Engineering
Asteria Retail

Attachment: service-inventory-template.csv (stub)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jared Singh <j.singh@asteria-retail.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trace-to-Alert activation: Observability & Ops activation plan

Markus / team —

Couple of technical clarifications and a short plan from our implementation side:

1) Tracing hooks: the attached patch contains shim snippets for Node (OpenTelemetry auto-instrument + manual span wrappers), Go (otel/http middleware example), and a Python decorator for batch jobs. We keep span names stable: service.operation.resource — avoids churn when we route by span name. The shims are intentionally minimal so you can wire them in during canary rollout.

2) Dashboard templates: Redwood provides Grafana/Datadog JSON templates. We’ll pre-populate panels for:
   - request rate / p50-p99 latency per endpoint
   - error rate (4xx, 5xx) with anomaly detection baseline
   - KV cache hit-rate (if applicable)
   - model inference tail latency (for any services calling Redwood)

3) Error taxonomy: draft categories we recommend: client_error, transient_dependency, model_regression, config_misroute, infra_outage. Routing rules map taxonomy -> PagerDuty -> Slack channel -> runbook. We’ll circulate a one-page taxonomy doc for signoff before alert wiring.

4) Runbooks: Neha will own authoring templates (playbooks include triage checklist, rollback steps, owner contacts). We’ll attach the runbook template to the Jira ticket OPS-1129.

Action items assigned:
- Jared: upload service inventory and PD team (due Mon 17 May)
- Markus: confirm kickoff invite (tentatively Tue 18 May 10:00 PT)
- Neha: create OPS-1129 and attach runbook-template.md (ETA Mon 17 May)

Laura
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook-template.md (1.2kB), tracing_hooks_v1.patch (re-attached)

From: Jared Singh <j.singh@asteria-retail.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@asteria-retail.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trace-to-Alert activation: Observability & Ops activation plan

Thanks — quick follow-ups after we reviewed the attachments:

- Tracing: looks language-agnostic enough — we’ll roll Node & Go first and do Python after the batch window.
- PagerDuty: team alias "Retail-Platform-Prod" is live; escalation policy attached. Confirming we want pages to go to on-call only for taxonomy categories: model_regression and infra_outage. The rest should notify but not page.
- Compliance: retention policy is 90 days for traces, 1 year for logs. No PII expected in traces after our sanitizers.

Can you confirm: will Redwood’s dashboards include example alert thresholds or do you prefer we propose thresholds based on our traffic? We’d like Redwood to propose initial thresholds and we’ll tune after a week.

Also — I created a short doc with our SSO team details and a shared Drive folder (link below).

Priya and I will attend Tue 18 May 10:00 PT.

Jared

Attachments: pd-escalation-retail-platform-prod.json, asteria-sso-details.pdf

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Singh <j.singh@asteria-retail.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 07:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trace-to-Alert activation: Observability & Ops activation plan

Jared / Priya — great, thanks for the quick turns. Confirming items below and next steps:

- Kickoff call confirmed: Tue 18 May 10:00–10:30 PT (meeting invite sent).
- Redwood will propose initial alert thresholds for model_regression and infra_outage ahead of the call.
- Neha created OPS-1129 and attached the runbook template + onboarding checklist: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/OPS-1129
- I’ve also dropped the shared runbook folder here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-observability-playbooks (you should have access; tell me if not).

On the kickoff call we’ll:
1) Walk the service inventory and map owners
2) Roll the Node shim into one canary service (non-prod flag)
3) Load the dashboard templates into your Datadog instance for review
4) Review taxonomy and initial alert thresholds for signoff

If that all looks good I’ll send status updates after each milestone and schedule the simulated paging exercise for Week 3.

Thanks,
Markus

Attachments: redwood-observability-kickstart-checklist.pdf (re-attached)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jared Singh <j.singh@asteria-retail.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trace-to-Alert activation: Observability & Ops activation plan

Thanks all — I’ve created OPS-1129 and assigned initial tasks. I’ll shepherd runbook drafts and coordinate the simulated paging exercise.

Small note: I’ll need owner contact emails for each service in the inventory so runbook pages contain direct contacts. Jared — can you add owner email column to the CSV?

See you on the call.

Neha
Implementation Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
